question: Which is NOT included in COGS for a manufacturing company?
before: CEO salary is SGA expense, not direct production cost. Raw materials, factory wages, factory utilities are all direct production costs in COGS.
after:
Concept: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) comprises all direct costs incurred to manufacture a product — raw materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead. Indirect expenses related to running the business (administration, sales, management) are classified as Selling, General & Administrative (SG&A) expenses and appear below the gross profit line on the income statement.

Why this is correct: CEO salary is a corporate overhead and administrative expense, not a direct cost of manufacturing. It does not vary with production volume and is classified as SG&A, appearing as an operating expense separate from COGS.

Why the others are wrong: Option A (raw material cost) is the fundamental input to production and forms the largest component of COGS. Option B (factory workers wages) is direct labor — the cost of workers whose time is directly tied to making the product. Option D (factory electricity bill) is manufacturing overhead — a facility cost directly attributable to the production process.

Intuition: In equity research, COGS represents the true economic cost of manufacturing each unit sold. CEO pay is a fixed corporate overhead that does not change if you produce 100 units or 1,000 units, so analysts exclude it from COGS when calculating gross margin. Gross margin (revenue minus COGS) reveals production efficiency; operating margin (gross profit minus SG&A) shows how well management controls overhead. Confusing the two masks the underlying operational picture.
